company_items.summary: AutoZone beat FQ4 EPS estimates with $56.05 vs. the Street's $54.03, but the quality was poor — the upside was driven by tariff refunds (145 basis point GM tailwind) and a non-cash LIFO benefit (105 basis point GM tailwind). Domestic comps missed badly at +1.6% vs. the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced an acquisition of RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex more aggressively in the Physical AI and robotics perception space.

MillerKnoll posted solid FQ1 EPS of 53 cents vs. the Street's 36 cents, and notably would have beaten even excluding the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind (adjusted EPS of 42 cents still topped consensus). Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million vs. the Street's $943.2 million, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed to $3.88–4.03 billion from $3.93–4.13 billion, while EPS guidance was left unchanged at $1.85–2.15.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1st, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. This is a leadership change with no financial results attached.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS estimates with 78 cents vs. the Street's 87 cents, as gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% versus the Street's 13.85% estimate. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation pressuring household budgets throughout the key selling season, and noted rising material costs hit margins hard. Some bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost reduction actions underway, and a roughly 75% year-over-year surge in the North American towable RV order backlog — though the company will not provide formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. This is a significant readout for the company as it competes in the high-stakes obesity drug market. The result is a major positive catalyst for the stock.

sectors: The RV sector faces ongoing macro headwinds per THOR Industries — stubborn interest rates, fuel costs, and inflation are keeping retail soft. The GLP-1/obesity drug space gets a fresh positive data point from Viking. Robotics and Physical AI M&A activity continues with the Cognex-RealSense deal.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This morning's note is purely company-specific — there's no broad macro or index-level commentary, so let's go straight through the earnings and events that matter today.

Starting with AutoZone, which reported fiscal fourth-quarter earnings of $56.05 per share, topping the Street's $54.03 estimate. But don't get too excited about the beat — it was low quality. The upside came from tariff refunds, which added 145 basis points to gross margins, and a non-cash LIFO benefit worth another 105 basis points. Strip those out and the picture is less flattering. Domestic comps came in at plus 1.6%, well short of the plus 3.1% the Street was looking for, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management did say linearity improved as the quarter progressed and they feel well positioned for fiscal 2027 sales growth, but this is a mixed result at best.

MillerKnoll is a cleaner beat. They earned 53 cents in fiscal Q1 versus the Street's 36-cent estimate, and critically, they would have beaten even without the tariff refund tailwind — stripping out that 11-cent benefit still leaves 42 cents versus a 36-cent consensus. Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923 million, but orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year sales guidance was trimmed modestly while EPS guidance was held steady. Net positive.

THOR Industries is the clear disappointment this morning. Fiscal Q4 EPS came in at 78 cents versus the Street's 87-cent estimate, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%. Management was candid about the environment — stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation are squeezing household budgets and keeping retail soft. They won't give formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall. There were some silver linings — dealer inventory is healthy, structural cost cuts are underway, and the North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year-over-year — but overall this is a cautious and disappointing print.

Cognex is acquiring RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and Physical AI, for roughly $500 million upfront plus another $106 million. RealSense is expected to do $80 to $90 million in revenue, growing more than 50% year-over-year. This is a bold move into the Physical AI buildout theme.

And the most exciting development this morning is Viking Therapeutics, whose shares are spiking pre-market after reporting 22% weight loss in trial results for their GLP-1 drug VK2735. This is a major positive data readout in one of the hottest therapeutic areas in the market right now.

Pentair named a new CFO, Bob Hau, effective November first — he's got prior CFO stints at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox. Routine leadership transition, nothing dramatic.

Bottom line for today: Viking is the high-energy trade in biotech, THOR is a macro warning sign for the consumer discretionary and RV space, and AutoZone's beat deserves scrutiny given the tariff-driven quality issues. Stay sharp.
